changes: Revise offline risk only: reduce fixed decision-close budget from 500 to 250 dollars. Retain r10>0.006 and r5>0 entry gate, 21-close warmup, 1.10 uncertain-fill buffer, ten-decimal quantity rounding, 10bp fee and 5bp slippage. Metadata rewritten to identify this offline revision rather than inherit old adoption claims. Exact match-2 parent preserved byte-for-byte. No infrastructure, live orders, or real trading changed; one candidate evaluated.
hypothesis: On the reused public t=0..59 development data, cutting only the decision-close budget from 500 to 250 dollars with unchanged entry gates will improve mean net episode profit, reduce worst loss and maximum marked drawdown to at most 51% of parent, and leave entry counts unchanged with zero rejected fills, over all t=20..52 paired episodes. Otherwise retain the parent. This is a risk-reduction hypothesis, not improved timing or alpha.
provenance: Public match-2 scoreboard and previous own metrics reviewed before declaring this single hypothesis in hypothesis-before-replay.json. Already published 60-bar t=0..59 dataset copied unchanged from match-1/agent-one/public-bars.csv; reused development data, not fresh or held-out evidence. At t=20..52 both independently compiled executables receive only t=0..t public prefixes; evaluator alone uses already-public t+1..t+7 closes. No private judge data, unseen observations or t>=60 prices used. Independent matched judge replay is unavailable. All results agent-run, not judge verified. Later adaptation remains allowed with truthful provenance.
result_interpretation: 33 paired reset episodes: mean profit old -1.3252441858250719 dollars, new -0.662622092910052; worst profit -31.912713903428653 versus -15.956356951419139 dollars; maximum marked drawdown 3.1912713903428654% versus 1.595635695141914%. Six entries each, zero rejected fills. Declared risk criterion passed. Five stride-seven descriptive episodes: mean profit -1.7701091581125639 versus -0.8850545791014156 dollars. Both main means remain negative and below the local benchmark mean -0.08407143005915645 dollars. Risk reduction is essentially mechanical, not new predictive edge. Upside capture is also reduced; no future superiority is claimed.
review: Match-2 scoreboard: equity 970.5717805885888, profit -29.42821941141119 (-2.9428219411%), one trade, zero failures, maximum round marked drawdown 2.9428219411%. Benchmark equity 934.3737786472714, return -6.5626221353%; own benchmark gap +3.6198001941 percentage points. Relative outperformance did not prevent absolute loss. Weaknesses: trend entry can buy a failed rally, fixed half-capital exposure magnifies loss, and the previous public replay already had negative mean profit. One match and reused historical episodes do not establish predictive skill. Review uses public scoreboard only; independent matched judge replay is unavailable.
shared_tips: For the other agent: evaluate absolute loss and marked drawdown alongside benchmark-relative return, because beating a falling benchmark can still lose capital.
For the other agent: separate exposure changes from signal changes in paired replays; smaller positions mechanically shrink both gains and losses and should not be mistaken for improved alpha.

For the other agent: use identical prefix-only inputs, warmup, next-close fills and transaction costs, and label reused overlapping windows as development data; execution mismatches and dependent observations can create false confidence.
For the other agent: count all-or-none cash rejections explicitly and keep leverage prohibited; a decision-price sizing buffer is only a heuristic because an unknown next close can gap.
